column1: Using CPI in Loss Given Default Forecasting Models

The thesis titled Using CPI in Loss Given Default Forecasting Models for Commercial Real Estate Portfolio by Ying Wu  Garvit Arora  and Xuan Mei  explores the challenges and solutions in forecasting the loss given default (LGD) for defaulted Commercial Real Estate (CRE) loans. The authors highlight the difficulty in predicting LGD due to the extended resolution and workout time associated with CRE defaults  especially within the frameworks of the Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review (CCAR) and the Current Expected Credit Loss (CECL) standards. These frameworks restrict the use of post-default information  including macroeconomic variables (MEVs) such as unemployment rates and various interest rates  which adds to the uncertainty in predictive LGD models.

The paper addresses the current environment of persistent inflation and elevated rates  which further complicates LGD predictions. The authors propose leveraging both internal and public data sources  including observations from the COVID-19 period  to demonstrate that the growth rates of the Consumer Price Index (CPI)  such as Year-over-Year (YoY) growth and logarithmic growth  serve as effective leading indicators for various CRE-related rates and indices. These include the Federal Funds Effective Rate and CRE market sales price indices in key locations like Los Angeles  New York  and nationwide  covering both apartment and office segments.

The authors argue that incorporating CPI at the time of default can enhance the accuracy of predicting CRE workout LGD. This approach is particularly beneficial in addressing the common issue of early downturn underestimation encountered in CRE LGD models. The paper emphasizes the importance of CPI as a leading indicator of future rates and CRE market sales prices  which can help mitigate the early downturn LGD underestimation issue  especially for the CTL portfolio covered by the authors.

The thesis is structured to first introduce the CRE CTL portfolio within JPMorgan Chase (JPMC)  which engages in long-term  permanent mortgage financing on stabilized income-producing CRE. The majority of loans are for multifamily lending (MFL) property types  with JPMC being the nation's largest multifamily lender. The authors  part of the Wholesale Credit QR team at JPMC  are responsible for developing loss forecast models compliant with CCAR and CECL frameworks  including probability of default (PD) and LGD models.

The paper then delves into the challenges of LGD modeling  highlighting two main issues: the left-censoring of LGD data due to CECL and CCAR rules requiring non-negative LGD values  and the restriction on using post-default MEVs in LGD models. The authors propose using CPI as a leading indicator to address these challenges  noting that few existing LGD models have explored this approach.

The thesis concludes by presenting statistical and machine learning evidence supporting the inclusion of CPI in CRE CTL LGD models  demonstrating its effectiveness in improving prediction accuracy and addressing early downturn underestimation. The authors aim to share their findings with researchers interested in this topic  contributing to the broader understanding of LGD modeling in the context of commercial real estate.
